learning_outcomes.text: Students learn to calculate the forces acting at bearing and connection points, at smooth and friction-affected contact points of systems, and within the structural elements themselves for technical load-bearing structures designed as two- and three-dimensional multi-part rigid body systems.

syllabus_topics: Calculation of forces in technical load-bearing systems
Decomposition of technical load-bearing systems into individual components or suitable substructures
Identification of interacting forces between elements through free-body diagrams
Setting up systems of equations for friction and equilibrium conditions
Solving equation systems to determine magnitudes and directions of forces
Application of acquired knowledge to determine mechanical stresses on machine elements and components of technical products
Selection, design, and dimensioning of elements based on loads
Verification of strength and service life of elements

assessment_methods.method: passing multiple homework assignments distributed over the semester with at least 75% of the total achievable score (Prüfungsvorleistung XP)

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on a graded written exam of 120 minutes. A prerequisite for taking the exam is passing multiple homework assignments distributed over the semester with at least 75% of the total achievable score. The exam directly after the first semester is mandatory (Terminfach).
bibliography: Gross, D.; Hauger, W.; Schröder, J., Wall, W. A.: Technische Mechanik 1 	 Statik. Springer 2006
